framework.title: Elhage, Nanda, Olsson et al. (2021), A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits
framework.claims: Verified quotes: "The residual stream is simply the sum of the output of all the previous layers and the original embedding"; "the residual stream doesn't have a 'privileged basis'; we could rotate it by rotating all the matrices interacting with it, without changing model behavior"; W_O W_V and W_Q^T W_K "can always be thought of as individual, low-rank matrices"; "The OV and QK matrices are extremely low-rank. They are 50,000 × 50,000 matrices, but only rank d_head (64 or 128)"; the SVD of W_OV: right singular vectors describe the subspace "read in", left singular vectors the subspace written to.

toy.title: Elhage, Hume, Olsson, Schiefer et al. (2022), Toy Models of Superposition
toy.claims: Verified quotes: toy models "investigate how and when models represent more features than they have dimensions. We call this phenomenon superposition"; "Superposition simply means that there are more features than dimensions"; "Although it's only possible to have n orthogonal vectors in an n-dimensional space, it's possible to have exp(n) many 'almost orthogonal' (< ε cosine similarity) vectors in high-dimensional spaces", citing the Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma. The course quotes the definitions and the geometric fact; it makes no claim about which features GPT-2 holds in superposition.

3b1b.title: Grant Sanderson, Essence of linear algebra (video series, 16 chapters), 3blue1brown.com
3b1b.claims: Verified on 2026-10-20 by opening each lesson page: chapter numbers and titles 1 Vectors, what even are they?; 2 Linear combinations, span, and basis vectors; 3 Linear transformations and matrices; 4 Matrix multiplication as composition; 5 Three-dimensional linear transformations; 6 The determinant; 7 Inverse matrices, column space, and null space; 8 Nonsquare matrices as transformations between dimensions; 9 Dot products and duality; 10 Cross products; 11 Cross products in the light of linear transformations; 12 Cramer's rule, explained geometrically; 13 Change of basis; 14 Eigenvectors and eigenvalues; 15 A quick trick for computing eigenvalues; 16 Abstract vector spaces. The series has no chapter on SVD, PCA, least squares, or gradients.

arena.title: ARENA curriculum (learn.arena.education): Chapter 0 Fundamentals and Chapter 1 Transformer Interpretability
arena.claims: Verified on 2026-10-20: Chapter 0 sections 0.0 Prerequisites ("Essential PyTorch basics, einops/einsum libraries, and tensor manipulation fundamentals"), 0.1 Ray Tracing ("Learn batched operations and linear algebra by rendering 3D meshes"); Chapter 1 sections 1.1 Transformers from Scratch, 1.2 Intro to Mech Interp (TransformerLens, hooks), 1.3.1 Linear Probes, 1.3.2 Function Vectors & Model Steering, 1.3.3 Interpretability with SAEs, 1.4.1 Indirect Object Identification, 1.5.4 Superposition & SAEs ("Replicate Anthropic's superposition paper"). Section numbers are as shown on that date; ARENA renumbers between iterations.

np-svd.title: NumPy reference: numpy.linalg.svd
np-svd.claims: Verified: returns U, S, Vh with singular values "sorted in descending order"; with full_matrices=False the shapes are (M, K) and (K, N) with K = min(M, N) and a == (u * s) @ vh.

np-lstsq.title: NumPy reference: numpy.linalg.lstsq
np-lstsq.claims: Verified: computes x that minimises the Euclidean 2-norm of b − a x; "If there are multiple minimizing solutions, the one with the smallest 2-norm is returned"; residuals is an empty array when rank(a) < N or M <= N.

np-eigh.title: NumPy reference: numpy.linalg.eigh
np-eigh.claims: Verified: for a real symmetric (or Hermitian) matrix, returns eigenvalues "in ascending order" and eigenvectors as columns; only one triangle of the input is read, so it does not check symmetry.

np-einsum.title: NumPy reference: numpy.einsum
np-einsum.claims: Verified: "Evaluates the Einstein summation convention on the operands"; np.einsum('ij,jk', a, b) is matrix multiplication, np.einsum('i,i', a, b) is the inner product, np.einsum('ii', a) is the trace.
